title: Design v2: design review feedback round 2 (hero, gallery, steps, deploy, import)
description:
Open-source contribution opportunity. Repository: accordproject/template-playground. Labels: enhancement, help wanted. Design review feedback on the Design v2 layout, gathered against the deploy preview of #980 (https://deploy-preview-980--ap-template-playground.netlify.app/, with **Settings → Enable New Design** switched on). Builds on #963 / #978 / #980 — please branch from the #980 branch or from `main` once it has merged.

All user-facing copy lives in `src/components/designV2/constants.ts`; step order/labels are in `STEPS` (`src/types/designV2.types.ts`); views are in `src/components/designV2/`.

Docs links referenced below were checked on 2026-09-14.

---

## 1. Hero copy — align with public messaging

`WELCOME.titleLine` / `titleAccent` / `subtitleLine1` / `subtitleLine2`. Current:

> **Contracts that run themselves.**
> Write the agreement once — as text, data and rules — and watch it execute. Six steps, no setup.

"Run themselves" over-promises and doesn't match how the docs site describes the project. Public messaging to align with (docs home, [Overview](https://docs.accordproject.org/docs/accordproject/), [Agentic Commerce](https://docs.accordproject.org/docs/accordproject-agentic-commerce)):

- "Smart Legal Contracts, Open Source"
- "Legal text drafted by lawyers, interpreted by courts, and executable by software — from the same open source template."
- "agreements that can be read and interpreted by people and courts, *and* executed by machines"
- "The enforceable-terms layer for autonomous commerce" / "Accord Project is the **agreement** layer"

Chosen replacement (title line / accent / subtitle):

> **The agreement layer for agentic commerce.**
> Write enforceable terms that humans read and software executes. Build, test and deploy a template in your browser.

Other candidates considered, for reference:

| # | Title | Accent | Subtitle |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | Agreements that | people sign and machines run. | Text, data and logic in one open source template — readable by lawyers, executable by software. Build one in six steps, no setup. |
| B | Contracts that | agents can execute. | Define the terms once — as text, data and rules — and let people, courts and AI agents all work from the same template. |
| C | The agreement layer | for agentic commerce. | Write enforceable terms that humans read and software executes. Build, test and deploy a template in your browser. |
| D | Legal text that | executes. | Drafted by lawyers, interpreted by courts, run by software — from the same open source template. Six steps, no setup. |

- [ ] Set `WELCOME.titleLine` = "The agreement layer", `titleAccent` = "for agentic commerce.", `subtitleLine1` = "Write enforceable terms that humans read and software executes.", `subtitleLine2` = "Build, test and deploy a template in your browser."

## 2. "How it works" → docs site

`WELCOME.howItWorks` currently navigates in-app to `ROUTES.learnIntro` (`/learn/intro`). It should open the docs site explanation in a new tab instead — the ↗ glyph already implies an external link.

- [ ] Point the button at https://docs.accordproject.org/docs/accordproject-template/ (Templates: text / model / logic) — or https://docs.accordproject.org/docs/accordproject/ if we'd rather land on the overview. Add the URL to `URLS`.

## 3. Template gallery — three representative real-world templates

The three cards (Counter Contract, Employment Offer, Non-disclosure; `src/samples/*`, `SampleArt.tsx`) currently read as engine feature demos ("init() and trigger()", "Enforces a maximum"). They should be:

- representative of real agreements a user would recognise, and
- each chosen to show a **different template feature** (e.g. one text-only / variables, one with a model + conditional/formatted text, one with stateful logic and requests), so the cards double as a tour of what a template can do.

Counter Contract in particular is not a real agreement and should be replaced. Rewrite the tagline and three bullet points on each card in agreement language rather than API language.

- [ ] Replace the three samples with realistic agreements, each illustrating a distinct feature set
- [ ] Rewrite taglines/bullets accordingly; update card illustrations in `SampleArt.tsx`

## 4. "Start from blank" as a card

`START.blank` ("+ Start blank") is a small button in the top-right of the gallery header. Make it a fourth card in the grid, styled like the template cards (illustration, "Blank template" title, a one-line tagline, its own "Start with this template →" button), so the choice reads as one set of options.

- [ ] Render "Start blank" as a gallery card; remove the header button

## 5. Rename "Model & Data" → "Data"

Step 3 label in the stepper (`STEPS` in `src/types/designV2.types.ts`), plus the step heading in `ModelDataView.tsx` ("Define the model and fill in the data") and anywhere else the phrase appears (Logic step "Request & Response types" row links back to it; the `THIS STEP NEEDS` checklist; tests). The `model.cto · data.json` meta line can stay.

- [ ] Rename step label and heading; grep for "Model & Data" in `src/components/designV2` and `src/tests`

## 6. Simulate — less technical wording

Stepper subtitle for step 5 is "run requests" (`STEPS[…].meta`). Within the step: "New request", "▶ Send", "▶ Init contract", "Pick a run on the left to see its request and response." Replace "request"/"run requests" with plainer language, e.g. "try it out", "send a message", "trigger the contract". Suggested: stepper meta **"try it out"**; "New request" → **"Send a message to the contract"**.

- [ ] Reword Simulate step copy (`SIMULATE` constants / `SimulateView.tsx`)

## 7. Text step — "Why this step" copy

`TextView.tsx` "WHY THIS STEP" text. Replace:

> This is what a human signs. Every variable resolves against the model, so a typo surfaces here long before a run.

with:

> This is what a human signs or an agent reads. Every variable resolves against the data model, so a typo surfaces here long before execution.

- [ ] Update the string

## 8. Remove the "Apply & Compile" button

The Logic step footer has "Apply & Compile" (`FOOTER.applyAndCompile` / `applyAndCompileDirty`; `LogicView.tsx`, `DesignV2Layout.tsx`). Users shouldn't need an explicit compile action — compile implicitly when leaving the Logic step (on **Next →** / clicking the Simulate step), and show compile errors in the problems pill / checklist. The "Simulate can't run yet … hit Apply & Compile" dialog then needs rewording (or goes away, since arriving at Simulate triggers the compile).

- [ ] Compile on transition Logic → Simulate; remove the footer button
- [ ] Update the "Simulate can't run yet" dialog copy and the related tests

## 9. Deploy step — more options, each with a description

`DEPLOY.cards` is currently `["Download PDF", "Share link", "Copy to clipboard"]` — bare titles with no explanation. Every card (existing and new) should carry a one-line description under its title so a user can tell what it does and where it takes them. Proposed set:

| Card | Description | Action / link |
|---|---|---|
| Download PDF | Save the rendered agreement as a PDF to share or sign. | existing |
| Share link | Copy a link that opens this template in the Playground. | existing |
| Copy to clipboard | Copy the rendered agreement text. | existing |
| Download template archive | Save the template as a `.cta` archive you can version, publish or load anywhere Accord Project tooling runs. | Download the current template as a `.cta` archive |
| Deploy to an APAP server | Publish the template to an Agreement Protocol server so apps and services can create and trigger agreements over REST. | Link to https://docs.accordproject.org/docs/ref-apap/#deploy-a-template (tutorial: https://docs.accordproject.org/docs/tutorial-apap/) |
| Embed in your app | Use the template engine from your own code to draft, validate and execute this template. | Link to https://github.com/accordproject/template-engine#readme (`URLS.engineDocs` already exists); swap for a docs page if one is added |
| Deploy to an MCP server | Expose the template to AI assistants (Claude, Cursor, …) through the Model Context Protocol endpoint of an APAP server. | Link to https://docs.accordproject.org/docs/ref-apap/#mcp-support-experimental |

Cards that only link out should open the docs in a new tab and carry the ↗ glyph. Change `DEPLOY.cards` from a string array to `{ title, description, href? }` objects.

- [ ] Add descriptions to the three existing cards
- [ ] Add the four new cards (link-out cards can ship first; `.cta` download needs a small export helper)

## 10. Preview button placement

`HEADER.preview` ("◧ Preview") is a small toggle in the top-right of the header, easy to miss. Preview matters most while editing text and data, so make it a prominent control on the **Text** and **Data** steps (e.g. a primary button in the step header next to the editor toolbar, or a split-pane toggle) rather than a global header affordance.

- [ ] Move/duplicate the Preview control into the Text and Data step views and make it visually primary

## 11. Importing templates

The gallery only offers the bundled samples. We need ways to bring in a template from elsewhere — probably as additional entry points on the Template step alongside the cards:

- [ ] **Import from the Accord Project template library** — browse/search https://templates.accordproject.org/ and load a template by name/version
- [ ] **Upload from disk** — a `.cta` archive (and ideally a template directory / zip)
- [ ] **Import from an external library** — a generic "load from URL" (`.cta` URL or a library index), so third-party template libraries can be used without code changes. Design the entry point so a named external library can be added later.

Each import should behave like "Start with this template": load the template + its sample and open the Text step.

---

Feedback captured with the maintainer during a live design review on 2026-09-14; ask in the comments if any item needs more context.

title: [Bug] Internal smali assembler silently emits invalid DEX when `.catch` regions are nested/overlapping
description:
Open-source contribution opportunity. Repository: REAndroid/APKEditor. Labels: bug, good first issue. **Describe the bug**
When rebuilding with `-dex-lib = internal` (the default), the smali assembler accepts nested (overlapping) `.catch` try-regions and emits the overlapping ranges verbatim as `try_item`s. The DEX spec requires try items within a `code_item` to be sorted, in-range and **non-overlapping** — so the produced dex is invalid.

Official smali (baksmali/smali, also used by apktool) supports nested `.catch` by flattening overlaps into disjoint try ranges with merged handler sets. APKEditor's internal assembler does neither: the build **succeeds with zero warnings** ("Saved to: …") and the invalid dex is shipped. On device, ART then refuses to open the whole dex file, so *every* class in that dex becomes unresolvable at runtime (`NoClassDefFoundError` on a perfectly valid, unrelated class). The `d` command happily disassembles such a file back — nothing in the toolchain ever complains.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Used version `APKEditor 1.4.9`, ARSCLib `1.3.9` **and** `1.4.0` (both affected), OpenJDK `26.0.1+8-34`, device Android 13
2. Operating system `Windows 11 x64`
3. Command — see attached `apkeditor-nestedcatch-repro.zip` (includes prebuilt `nested.apk` / `flat.apk` / `nested_jf.apk`):
```
build_repro.bat <path-to-apkeditor.jar>
```
It builds two ready-made mini projects (identical semantics, different catch layout) and validates the produced dexes with `dexcheck.py` (standalone, no deps):

* `mini_nested/` — one class, one method, outer `.catch` region fully containing an inner one (legal smali):
```smali
    :try_outer
    invoke-static {p0}, Landroid/graphics/Color;->parseColor(Ljava/lang/String;)I
    ...
    :try_inner
    invoke-static {p1}, Ljava/lang/Float;->parseFloat(Ljava/lang/String;)F
    :try_end_inner
    .catch Ljava/lang/Throwable; {:try_inner .. :try_end_inner} :inner_label
    :inner_label
    ...
    :try_end_outer
    .catch Ljava/lang/Throwable; {:try_outer .. :try_end_outer} :outer_label
```
* `mini_flat/` — same code split into two disjoint regions (the workaround).

Observed output:
```
=== nested ===
00.465 I: [BUILD] Saved to: nested.apk          (success, no diagnostic)
PROBLEMS (1):
  - LRepro;#0: try overlap/unsorted start=0 prev_end=13

=== flat ===
00.466 I: [BUILD] Saved to: flat.apk
STRUCTURE OK
```

**Log/Stacktrace**
Installing the nested variant's real-world counterpart (same construct inside an app's own class) on an Android 13 device:
```
FATAL EXCEPTION: main
java.lang.NoClassDefFoundError: Failed resolution of: Lf/a/a/a/a;
    at androidx.preference.PreferenceManager.getDefaultSharedPreferencesName(SourceFile:1)
    at androidx.preference.PreferenceManager.getDefaultSharedPreferences(SourceFile:1)
    ...
Caused by: java.lang.ClassNotFoundException: f.a.a.a.a
```
The class is present in the rebuilt dex's `class_defs` table (verified by direct dex parsing); the whole dex is simply rejected by ART because of the invalid try-item table. Replacing the nested regions with disjoint ones makes the identical app work.

**Used apk file**
Not shareable (proprietary, 169 MB). However the issue is fully reproducible without it — see the attached minimal reproduction project `apkeditor-nestedcatch-repro.zip` (~16 KB: mini projects, prebuilt apks, validator, one-click script, README).

**Additional context**
- Disjoint side-by-side `.catch` regions, and multiple handlers over one region, are handled fine — only genuinely nested/overlapping ranges produce the corrupt output.
- The tool's own `-dex-lib jf` (JesusFreke/smali) backend assembles the identical `mini_nested` source into 3 correctly flattened, non-overlapping try_items (`STRUCTURE OK`). So the expected behavior is implemented inside the same codebase; only the default `internal` assembler emits the overlap silently.
- Suggested fix: at minimum hard-error on overlapping catch regions (naming class/method/labels); ideally flatten them like official smali does.

[apkeditor-nestedcatch-repro.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32236495/apkeditor-nestedcatch-repro.zip)

[kgap-scan:scope] Neurodegenerative Diseases: Autophagy-Senescence-Inflammasome (ASI) axis as unified cross-disease mechanism
description:
Open-source contribution opportunity. Repository: monarch-initiative/dismech. Labels: help wanted, curation, high_effort, knowledge_gaps. ## Publication Details

**PMID:** 42419491  
**DOI:** 10.1016/j.arr.2026.103248  
**Title:** The Autophagy-Senescence-Inflammasome Axis: A Novel Triad in Neurodegenerative Diseases?  
**Publication Date:** 2026-07-08  
**Authors:** Ellappan S, Kujur PP, Mondal AC  
**Europe PMC:** https://europepmc.org/article/MED/42419491  
**PubMed:** https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42419491/  

## Gap Signal

**Explicitly stated gap:** "Chronic neuroinflammation is a defining feature of brain ageing and neurodegenerative disorders, yet the molecular mechanisms responsible for its persistence remain incompletely understood."

**Proposed unified mechanism:** The paper proposes an integrated Autophagy-Senescence-Inflammasome (ASI) axis where reciprocal interactions among impaired autophagy, senescent glia, and inflammasome signaling establish a self-sustaining cycle of neuroinflammation. The evidence spans Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, multiple sclerosis, stroke, and chronic neuropathic pain.

## Handoff Objective

**Scope:** Cross-disease mechanistic convergence affecting Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, ALS, MS, stroke, and neuropathic pain.

**Missing/uncertain mechanism objects:**
- The integrated ASI axis and its reciprocal feedback loops: how defective autophagy promotes mitochondrial dysfunction → oxidative stress → danger signaling → inflammasome activation, while senescent astrocytes/microglia amplify responses through SASP
- Mitochondrial dysfunction as the proposed central mechanistic hub linking all three processes
- Disease-specific vs. universal aspects of the ASI axis across different neurodegenerative conditions
- How upstream triggers (protein aggregation in AD/PD, excitotoxicity in ALS, demyelination in MS) feed into the ASI axis
- Therapeutic targeting of ASI axis components (autophagy enhancers, senolytic agents, inflammasome inhibitors) and their relative efficacy

**Question:** Should a dedicated module (e.g., \`autophagy_senescence_inflammasome_axis\`) be created to capture this cross-disease mechanistic convergence? Should existing disorder entries for ALS, PD, AD, MS incorporate conformance to this unified axis with their disease-specific triggering context? Are current entries separately documenting autophagy dysfunction, glial senescence, and inflammasome activation, or should this be integrated?

title: Verify the install path on OpenShift / OKD (no code required)
description:
Open-source contribution opportunity. Repository: MSKazemi/kubeintellect. Labels: help wanted, good first issue, area/deploy. **No code required. You need a OpenShift / OKD cluster and about an hour.**

CI runs every test on Kind only. Nobody has verified KubeIntellect on **OpenShift / OKD**, so we genuinely do not know whether it works there — and [ADOPTERS.md](https://github.com/MSKazemi/kubeintellect/blob/main/ADOPTERS.md) is honestly empty rather than padded.

## Why this platform

SecurityContextConstraints reject many manifests that work everywhere else — arbitrary UIDs and non-root enforcement are the usual break.

## What to do

Follow the documented install path on a OpenShift / OKD cluster and record what actually happens:

```bash
pip install kubeintellect
kubeintellect init            # setup wizard
kubeintellect serve           # API server on :8000
```

Then ask it something real about the cluster and try one **read-only** query end to end.

Report, as a comment on this issue:

1. **Platform + version** — `kubectl version`, distro/managed flavour, node count
2. **Did the documented steps work verbatim?** If not, the exact command and the exact error
3. **Any step the docs do not mention** but that turned out to be required
4. **Whether RBAC behaved** — a `readonly` key must be refused a mutating command *before* any approval prompt appears
5. **What you would change in the docs** — even one sentence

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A comment covering the five points above, with real command output
- [ ] Anything genuinely broken is filed as its own bug issue and linked here
- [ ] If the docs need a change, a PR to `v4/docs/` — **or** just say so and someone else can write it

A report saying **"it did not work, here is exactly where it stopped"** is more valuable than one saying it worked. That is the outcome we cannot get any other way.

⚠️ **Redact before pasting** — cluster output contains node names, namespaces and registries. And please use a **non-production cluster**, or a `readonly` key if it must be a real one.

## Credit

This counts. You are named in the release notes exactly like a code contributor
([GOVERNANCE.md](https://github.com/MSKazemi/kubeintellect/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md)), and if you
add yourself to [ADOPTERS.md](https://github.com/MSKazemi/kubeintellect/blob/main/ADOPTERS.md)
your environment becomes one of the ones we protect and keep backward-compatible.

*(Note: a comment alone will not appear on GitHub's Contributors graph, which counts merged
commits. A one-line docs PR from what you find will — and is usually warranted.)*

## Task metadata

| | |
|---|---|
| **Difficulty** | Beginner |
| **Estimated time** | ~1 hour |
| **Skills** | Kubernetes operations. Access to a OpenShift / OKD cluster. **No Python, no code.** |
| **Mentor** | @MSKazemi — ask on this issue, or in [Q&A](https://github.com/MSKazemi/kubeintellect/discussions/categories/q-a) |
| **Status** | 🟢 **Unclaimed** — comment "I'd like to take this" and it will be assigned to you |

title: [E8] checkowners explain and checkowners owners
description:
Open-source contribution opportunity. Repository: smusali/checkOwners. Labels: enhancement, help wanted, correctness. **Action item:** E8 · **Epic:** E — Drift, Generation, Validation, and Command Surface · **Priority:** P0 · **Effort:** M · **Milestone:** `0.6.0`
**Depends on:** C5, C6 · **Blocks:** M1
**Source:** `docs/PROJECT_STATE_AND_ROADMAP.md` §18.1, §33, §6.2

## Problem

Nothing lets a developer interrogate a score. `expertise <path>` ranks contributors but does not decompose the score, show the evidence behind each factor, name the commits involved, or explain why someone was *excluded*.

## Impact

This is the single highest-leverage UX improvement available, and probably the best-loved command the project could ship. **A confidence score you cannot interrogate is a score nobody trusts** — and a system that influences repository governance must never behave like an unexplained scoring black box. It is also the best possible demo recording.

## Scope of change

**`checkowners explain PATH`:**

```text
path/to/file.py

Observed owners
──────────────────────────────────────────────────
@alice                        0.86 confidence
  Recency 0.92   Frequency 0.81   Blame 0.89   Reviews 0.74
  37 commits · 68% current blame · 11 reviews
  last meaningful change: 12 days ago

@bob                          0.54 confidence
  Recency 0.33   Frequency 0.58   Blame 0.62   Reviews 0.71

Evidence quality:             0.91
Declared CODEOWNERS:          @company/platform
Team resolution:              @alice ∈ @company/platform, @bob ∈ @company/platform
Assessment:                   aligned
```

**The inverse form, which matters just as much:**

```text
$ checkowners explain path/to/file.py --why-not @carol

@carol was not inferred because:
- last contribution: 418 days ago
- 3% current blame
- no reviews in observation window
- confidence: 0.12 < threshold 0.30
```

**Required variants:** `explain FILE`, `explain DIRECTORY`, `explain FILE --owner @alice`, `explain FILE --why-not @bob`.

**`checkowners owners PATH`** (alias `who`) — the simplest question deserves the simplest command, with no analysis report:

```text
@alice  0.87
@bob    0.61
```

## Implementation notes

- Show per-signal contributions **and** availability (C5), so an unavailable signal is visibly different from a zero score.
- Name the specific commits behind each factor.
- State which configuration knobs would change the outcome — this is what makes the command actionable rather than merely informative.
- Show rename lineage (D3) when the path has prior names.
- Analyze only the evidence relevant to the requested path; do not run a full repository pass for a single-file question.
- Support `--json` for both commands.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `explain` decomposes every signal with score, weight, availability, and supporting evidence.
- [ ] `--why-not` explains exclusion with concrete numbers and the threshold that was missed.
- [ ] `--owner` scopes output to one contributor.
- [ ] Directory form aggregates sensibly and is documented.
- [ ] `owners` returns a minimal ranked list quickly.
- [ ] Neither command triggers a full-repository blame pass.
- [ ] Both support `--json`, schema-versioned per F2.
- [ ] Output states which configuration changes would alter the result.

## Test plan

- Fixture asserting the decomposition arithmetic matches the reported total exactly.
- `--why-not` for a contributor below threshold and for one who never touched the path — both must be explicable, not identical.
- Assert blame invocation count is proportional to the requested path, not the repository.
- Golden-file tests on rendered and JSON output.

## Documentation

`docs/USAGE.md`, `README.md`, `docs/METHODOLOGY.md`.

## Out of scope

Reviewer recommendation for a diff — that is E9.

title: Engineering Manager, Frontier AI Infrastructure - Public Sector
description: Organisation: Scale AI. Location: Washington, DC. Department: Public Sector Engineering. Office: Washington, DC. Scale AI’s Public Sector business is growing quickly as government agencies adopt AI to support critical national security, defense, and public sector missions. We are seeking a hands-on Engineering Manager to lead our Frontier AI Infrastructure team within Public Sector Engineering. This is a 50/50 role : you'll spend roughly half your time writing and reviewing code, and half your time leading, coaching, and growing a small team of engineers. title: Counsel review of the disclaimers before launch
description:
Open-source contribution opportunity. Repository: ChelseaKR/trans-docs-navigator. Labels: help wanted, roadmap, launch-gate. §10 of `docs/ROADMAP.md` recommends counsel review of the disclaimers **pre-launch**, on two distinct grounds:

- **Unauthorized practice of law** — the persistent "information, not legal advice" framing, the no-individualized-legal-conclusions rule, and the routing of edge cases to legal aid;
- **Privacy law** — the roadmap is explicit that the project must *not* claim CCPA/GDPR compliance **or exemption** without jurisdiction-specific counsel review, and must keep deletion instructions precise about local state and bounded server records.

This is a tool that tells trans people how to change their identity documents; the disclaimer language is part of the safety surface, not boilerplate.

*Imported from `docs/ROADMAP.md` §10 with AI assistance.*

title: Add privacy-preserving OpenTelemetry export
description:
Open-source contribution opportunity. Repository: Nhaooo/agent-company-core. Labels: help wanted, integration, security. ## Context

The framework records redacted audit events, but it does not export traces or metrics to OpenTelemetry. Operators would benefit from correlation across mission, provider, approval, and tool boundaries.

## Desired outcome

Add an optional observability integration that exports useful lifecycle signals while making data minimization the default.

## Scope

Define span and metric names, correlation identifiers, sampling behavior, and an allowlist for attributes. Never export prompts, model responses, credentials, raw tool arguments, or personal data by default.

## Acceptance criteria

- OpenTelemetry remains an optional extra and core imports stay provider-neutral.
- Exported attributes are allowlisted, documented, and tested for redaction.
- Provider failures, approvals, STOP, checkpoints, and tool outcomes can be correlated.
- Tests use an in-memory exporter and verify sensitive fields are absent.
- Security documentation explains deployment and retention assumptions.

## Relevant files/modules

- src/agent_company_core/observability/
- src/agent_company_core/orchestration/engine.py
- docs/security.md
- docs/integrations.md

## Testing expectations

Add unit tests for normal and failure paths, run pip-audit for the optional extra, and run the full existing suite.

## Estimated difficulty

Large; help wanted.

title: Add error monitoring and write an incident runbook
description:
Open-source contribution opportunity. Repository: mrpeanut01/elevator-sim. Labels: help wanted, qa, process, P1. ## Why

There is no error monitoring. If the deployed build throws in a player's browser, nobody finds out. That is survivable during development and is not survivable at launch.

The project has already shipped a defect of exactly this class: a boot failure where the page was dead and roughly two thousand tests were green. Nothing on the server side would have reported it.

## Scope

Add client error reporting and server error reporting, with sampling and with the privacy posture applied to whatever is captured. Then write the runbook: what pages, what the severity levels are, what the first response is, and how a rollback is triggered.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Client-side errors are reported, with the privacy posture applied
- [ ] Server-side errors and API failures are reported
- [ ] A verified alert path exists, tested by triggering a real error
- [ ] An incident runbook covering severity, first response and rollback
- [ ] A dead-page check that would have caught the historic boot failure

title: Performance: add a reproducible minimum-hardware local LLM benchmark suite
description:
Open-source contribution opportunity. Repository: sodejm/AncestryLLM. Labels: enhancement, help wanted. ## Context

The Python suite is fast (164 tests passed in 1.41 seconds during this audit), but there is no reproducible end-to-end benchmark for local model inference. The Ollama CLI is installed locally, but no server/model was running during the audit, so real inference latency, memory, and throughput could not be measured.

Without a controlled benchmark, tuning context, batching, parallelism, model quantization, prompt size, or keep-alive behavior is guesswork.

## Proposed work

- Add an opt-in benchmark harness that never downloads models and is excluded from normal unit-test CI.
- Use fictional/synthetic genealogy inputs for representative GEDCOM duplicate adjudication, RootsMagic interpretation, OCR post-processing, and quality-analysis workloads.
- Measure:
  - cold and warm model load latency
  - time to first token
  - prompt-evaluation tokens/second
  - generation tokens/second
  - total wall time
  - peak system RAM and VRAM when available
  - queue wait, cancellation, timeout, and unload behavior
- Compare the supported low-memory and balanced profiles across explicitly installed small quantized models.
- Store only aggregate, non-sensitive benchmark results and environment metadata.
- Add a concise operator report and machine-readable JSON output for future regression comparison.
- Coordinate framework/provider comparison with #24; this issue should benchmark the existing native adapters first.

## Acceptance criteria

- The harness exits with a clear skip when Ollama or a requested model is unavailable and never starts a download.
- Results record Ollama/model version, quantization, context size, profile, hardware summary, and cold/warm state.
- At least one documented minimum-hardware run establishes initial budgets for latency and peak memory.
- Release guidance defines how a material regression is triaged without making hardware-specific results block ordinary CI.
- Prompts and inputs are fictional and benchmark output passes repository artifact/privacy guards.
- Documentation explains how to reproduce results and compare changes fairly.

title: [P1] Persist JetBrains plugin settings across IDE restarts
description:
Open-source contribution opportunity. Repository: Sandesh13fr/TCalc. Labels: bug, help wanted, OSCI'26. ## Problem

The JetBrains plugin stores its configuration in an application service with mutable in-memory fields, but `WmaSettingsState` does not implement `PersistentStateComponent` and has no `@State`/`@Storage` declaration. Values entered under **Settings → Tools → TCalc** therefore return to defaults after the IDE restarts.

## Evidence

- `apps/jetbrains-plugin/src/main/kotlin/com/tcalc/plugin/settings/WmaSettingsState.kt` is only annotated with `@Service`.
- `WmaSettingsConfigurable.apply()` writes the Node path, CLI path, goal, privacy mode, and token budget only to that in-memory service.
- There is no persistence implementation or restart-level test in the plugin.

## Reproduction

1. Open Settings → Tools → TCalc.
2. Set a non-default CLI path, goal, or token budget and apply it.
3. Restart the IDE.
4. Reopen TCalc settings; the configured values are lost.

## Acceptance criteria

- Persist settings using the supported IntelliJ Platform state/storage APIs.
- Preserve all five current settings across IDE restarts.
- Keep defaults for a fresh installation and handle older/missing state safely.
- Add focused tests for state serialization/restoration or an equivalent persistence fixture.
- Document the manual restart verification and run the JetBrains plugin checks.

_No response_

title: Funding & Sustainability Plan
description:
Open-source contribution opportunity. Repository: ocftw/open-star-ter-village. Labels: enhancement, help wanted. ## Context

Open StarTer Village is planning to go online (see [Online Launch Plan #348](https://github.com/ocftw/open-star-ter-village/issues/348)), which will require sustained resources — server hosting, asset production, volunteer coordination, and potentially contracted development work. The project currently sits under [OCF (Open Culture Foundation)](https://ocf.tw/) as a community project, with [Friedrich Naumann Foundation (FNF)](https://www.freiheit.org/) as the original sponsor.

We need to clarify how funds can be raised, how they flow through OCF, and what sustainable models fit an open-source educational board game.

---

## Current Funding Landscape

| Aspect | Status |
|--------|--------|
| **Project owner** | OCF (財團法人開放文化基金會) — fiscal sponsor |
| **Original sponsor** | Friedrich Naumann Foundation (FNF) |
| **Donation channel** | OCF general donation page exists, but no project-specific channel |
| **Hosting costs** | Currently ~$0 (not deployed); Vercel free tier may suffice initially |
| **Ongoing costs** | Domain, hosting (if beyond free tier), asset production, event costs |

---

## Questions to Resolve

### 1. Fund Flow — How does money reach the project?
- [ ] Clarify OCF's fiscal sponsorship model for this project
  - Can earmarked donations go directly to Open StarTer Village?
  - What is OCF's overhead/admin fee structure for sponsored projects?
  - What spending requires OCF approval vs. project team discretion?
- [ ] Determine if the project needs its own sub-account or budget line within OCF
- [ ] Document the process: donor → OCF → project expenses (transparency)

### 2. Funding Sources — Where can money come from?

**Grants & Institutional Funding**
- [ ] **g0v Civic Tech Grant (公民科技獎助金)** — evaluate eligibility and application timeline
- [ ] **OCF internal resources** — does OCF allocate budget for its own community projects?
- [ ] **FNF renewed sponsorship** — explore continuing or expanding the existing FNF relationship
- [ ] **NLnet / Open Technology Fund** — European grants for open-source projects
- [ ] **Mozilla Foundation grants** — open-source education alignment
- [ ] **University partnerships** — USR (University Social Responsibility) course funding (the project already has university workshop experience)

**Community-Backed Funding**
- [ ] **GitHub Sponsors** — set up for `ocftw` org or individual maintainers
- [ ] **Open Collective** — transparent fund management, popular in open-source (would this complement or conflict with OCF's fiscal sponsorship?)
- [ ] **Crowdfunding campaign** (e.g., 嘖嘖 zeczec, Kickstarter) — best suited for Phase 3 (physical copies) as a milestone-based campaign; could bundle physical game + online access + supporter credits
- [ ] **Corporate sponsorship** — companies using the game for team building / onboarding; offer logo placement, custom card packs, or workshop facilitation

**In-Kind / Zero-Cost Resources**
- [ ] **Vercel / Netlify** — free tier or open-source sponsorship programs
- [ ] **Cloudflare** — free plan for the domain + CDN
- [ ] **Volunteer contributions** — the current backbone; formalize recognition
- [ ] **COSCUP / g0v hackathon** — development sprints at zero cost

### 3. Budget Estimation — What does it actually cost?

| Item | Estimated Cost | Phase |
|------|---------------|-------|
| Domain (openstartervillage.ocf.tw) | ~$0 (OCF subdomain) | Phase 1 |
| Vercel hosting (free tier) | $0 | Phase 1 |
| Vercel Pro (if needed) | ~$20/mo | Phase 1 |
| Fly.io game server (if needed) | ~$5–20/mo | Phase 1 |
| Tabletopia publisher account | $0 (free) | Phase 2 |
| Asset production (freelance designer) | $500–2,000 | Phase 1–2 |
| English rulebook translation | $300–800 (or volunteer) | Phase 2 |
| BGA development (contracted) | $3,000–10,000 (or volunteer) | Phase 3 |
| Physical print run (small batch) | $5,000–15,000 | Phase 3 |

### 4. Sustainability Model — Long-term
- [ ] Define the project's stance on monetization (free-to-play always? freemium? pay-what-you-want?)
- [ ] Sell physical copies while keeping digital free?
- [ ] Workshop/facilitation fees as a revenue stream?
- [ ] Establish transparent financial reporting (quarterly or per-phase)
- [ ] Plan for what happens if/when OCF can no longer host the project — succession plan for fiscal sponsorship

### 5. Relationship with Regional Communities
- [ ] How do partner communities (e.g., Japanese [ossquest.com](https://www.ossquest.com/)) fund their own activities? (see [#349](https://github.com/ocftw/open-star-ter-village/issues/349))
- [ ] Should regional partners handle their own hosting costs, or pool into a shared fund?
- [ ] Can regional partners independently seek local grants/sponsors under the same brand?

---

## Immediate Action Items

1. [ ] **Talk to OCF** — clarify fiscal sponsorship terms, earmarked donation options, and budget process for this project
2. [ ] **Estimate Phase 1 costs** — determine if free-tier hosting is sufficient or if we need funding before launch
3. [ ] **Set up GitHub Sponsors** — low effort, immediate visibility, good signal
4. [ ] **Draft a one-page sponsor deck** — for approaching corporate sponsors and grant applications
5. [ ] **Discuss at next Discord community meeting** — align contributors on funding philosophy (fully volunteer-driven vs. seeking grants)

title: Bot: SpecialHunterBot — values specials over goal progress
description:
Open-source contribution opportunity. Repository: RizgarOzan/match3-lab. Labels: good first issue, bot. The simulator has two bots: `random` (the floor) and `greedy` (goal progress first, then specials, then pieces cleared). There is nothing in between that answers *how much of greedy's win rate comes from chasing goals?*

Add `SpecialHunterBot`: like `GreedyBot.Evaluate`, but specials created weigh more than goal progress. Everything else — win bonus, loss penalty, one ply — stays.

**Interface** (`packages/com.rizgarozan.match3lab.core/Runtime/Simulation/IBot.cs`):
```csharp
public interface IBot
{
    string Name { get; }
    Move Choose(Game game, List<Move> legalMoves, Pcg32 rng);
}
```
Rules: deterministic (only the given `rng`), try moves on `game.CloneWithUnknownFuture(seed)` never `game.Clone()`, no `UnityEngine`. See [CONTRIBUTING.md → Adding a bot](https://github.com/RizgarOzan/match3-lab/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#adding-a-bot).

**Done when**
- `SpecialHunterBot` lives next to `GreedyBot`, name `special`
- `--bot special` works in `tools/Match3Lab.Cli/Program.cs`
- `BotTests.cs` has a test that the bot is deterministic for a seed and only returns legal moves
- the PR pastes `curve levels --bot special --runs 1000`

title: Add new fictional cases to the ledger (teaching and held-out)
description:
Open-source contribution opportunity. Repository: zgbrenner/thelegalfly. Labels: help wanted, good first issue. The evaluation is currently 32 teaching cases and 16 held-out cases. Sixteen is small enough that a single case moves the headline numbers (facts-only 14/16, biological MaleCNS 13/16, shuffled 11/16). More cases make the comparison between the connectome and its controls more meaningful.

**What a contribution looks like**

- One or more new petitions in `apps/web/public/legalfly/cases.json`, following the existing schema: petitioner, title, petition text, the eight facts (matter, property, harm, proof, intent, relationship, urgency, ability), and the charter action.
- A one-line note per case explaining why the label follows from the facts under the fictional village charter (see `docs/METHOD.md`). Cases whose label is not derivable from the eight facts are not useful to the fly and should not be added.
- Keep the village early-modern and fictional. No real people, real jurisdictions, or real legal advice.
- Run `npm test` and `npm run test:legalfly` in `apps/web`; the ledger validation test must still pass.

**Things to know**

- Adding cases changes the teaching set, so the readout retrains in the browser on every "Teach the ledger". That is expected.
- If you change the held-out split, say so in the PR and report the new scores for all five systems in the results table so the README can be updated honestly.

Establish strong security and access-management practices, including role-based access, segregation of duties, periodic reviews, and audit readiness. Lead Workday release planning by evaluating new functionality, assessing business impact, coordinating testing, documenting changes, and communicating recommendations to stakeholders. Maintain data integrity through proactive monitoring, recurring audits, reconciliation processes, and root-cause analysis of system or integration issues. Provide clear guidance and hands-on support to People team members, managers, employees, and business leaders. Create and maintain documentation for configurations, business processes, integrations, reports, controls, and user procedures. Build strong relationships with Workday, implementation partners, and other vendors while ensuring that Via retains clear internal ownership of its platform. Stay current on Workday capabilities, product releases, and industry practices, and help Via determine which improvements will deliver meaningful business value. You have deep experience with Core HCM and meaningful hands-on exposure across several additional Workday modules, such as Compensation, Recruiting, Benefits, Absence, Time Tracking, Performance, Talent, or Payroll. You understand how decisions in one Workday module can affect business processes, security, reporting, integrations, and downstream systems across the broader platform. You understand HR operations, payroll processes, compliance requirements, and the controls needed to support accurate and sensitive employee data. You can balance immediate business needs with long-term platform health, avoiding unnecessary customization and designing solutions that remain scalable and maintainable. You are comfortable advising senior stakeholders, challenging assumptions constructively, and translating complex technical topics into clear recommendations. You are highly detail-oriented, organized, and process-driven, with strong judgment and a clear sense of ownership. Experience helping an organization mature its Workday governance, architecture, documentation, security, or release-management practices. Advanced Workday reporting and analytics experience. Experience with Workday integration technologies such as EIB, Core Connectors, Workday Studio, APIs, or Workday Extend. Workday certifications across multiple functional or technical areas. title: Add keyboard navigation and ARIA labels to the board
description:
Open-source contribution opportunity. Repository: felipersteles/checkers-with-ai. Labels: enhancement, help wanted. ## Motivation
The board is only interactive via mouse/touch click (`CheckersGame._handleClick` in `game.js`), and squares/pieces have no `aria-*` attributes — the game is currently unusable for keyboard-only or screen-reader users.

## Proposal
Add keyboard navigation across board squares (arrow keys to move focus, Enter/Space to select/move) and appropriate ARIA roles/labels (e.g. `role="grid"`/`gridcell"`, `aria-label` describing each square's contents and coordinates) so the board is navigable and announced correctly by screen readers.

## Acceptance criteria
- The full board can be navigated and a legal move can be completed using only the keyboard.
- Screen readers announce square coordinates and piece presence/color/king status.
- Selected piece and legal destination squares are conveyed to assistive tech, not just via the `verde` CSS class.
- No regression to existing mouse/touch interaction.

title: Global Head of Payroll
description: Organisation: Via. Location: London. Department: People Operations. Office: London, New York City. Via is on a mission to create public transportation systems that provide far greater access to jobs, healthcare, and education. Our platform serves as the technology backbone for modern transit networks, transforming antiquated and siloed public transportation systems into smart, data-driven, and efficient digital networks. With hundreds of agency partners around the world, Via is recognized as the leading transportation technology and service provider globally. As Global Head of Payroll , you will lead and scale payroll operations across our global footprint, ensuring accurate, compliant, and timely payroll delivery for employees across the United States, Europe, Israel, and other international markets supported through employer-of-record (EOR) and payroll partners. This role is responsible for global payroll strategy, payroll operations, compliance, vendor management, and payroll technology. You will build and develop a high-performing global payroll organization, establish scalable processes and controls, and serve as a key partner to the Finance, Legal, People, and Operations teams. Success in this role requires a hands-on leader who can operate strategically while remaining close to the details, driving operational excellence in a fast-paced, high-growth, and globally distributed environment. What You'll Do Lead global payroll operations across all countries and entities, ensuring timely, accurate, and compliant payroll processing. Manage, coach, and develop a team of Payroll Managers and payroll professionals across multiple regions. Establish scalable payroll governance, controls, policies, and operating procedures that support a growing global workforce. Own relationships with global payroll providers, Employer of Record partners, tax advisors, and other payroll vendors, ensuring service quality, accountability, and continuous improvement. Partner closely with People Operations to ensure the accurate and timely flow of employee data, including new hires, terminations, compensation changes, benefits, leave programs, equity transactions, and organizational changes. Partner with Finance, Accounting, Tax, Equity Administration, and Legal to ensure compliance with global payroll regulations and reporting requirements. Ensure accurate processing and reporting of equity compensation, including RSUs, stock options, and related payroll tax obligations. Drive payroll technology strategy and optimization, including Workday Payroll, global payroll platforms like P&I Loga and iiPay, integrations, automation, reporting, and system implementations. Develop meaningful payroll metrics, dashboards, and reporting packages, including headcount reporting, payroll spend analysis, variance analysis, payroll tax reporting, and executive-level reporting. Ensure accurate and timely payroll tax filings, registrations, remittances, garnishments, and statutory reporting requirements globally. Identify opportunities to streamline processes, improve controls, reduce risk, and enhance the employee payroll experience. Serve as the senior escalation point for complex payroll matters and drive timely resolution of payroll-related issues. Who You Are Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or a related field. 10+ years of progressive payroll leadership experience, including responsibility for multinational payroll operations. Demonstrated experience leading global payroll teams across multiple countries and regions. Strong understanding of payroll taxes, financial controls, and payroll compliance. Proven ability to build scalable payroll processes and lead through periods of growth, change, and system transformation. Strong project management skills with experience managing multiple priorities and stakeholders simultaneously. Hands-on leadership style with a willingness to dive into operational details when needed. Exceptional analytical, problem-solving, and process improvement capabilities. Excellent communication skills and ability to influence stakeholders across all levels of the organization. High degree of discretion and commitment to maintaining confidentiality. What Catches Our Eye Experience with Workday, global payroll platforms (iiPay, P&I Loga, Malam, or similar) Experience supporting publicly traded companies and equity compensation payroll processing. Experience leading payroll transformations, implementations, and integration projects. Familiarity with SOX controls, public company reporting requirements, and audit environments. Experience building and mentoring high-performing payroll teams. Compensation and Benefits: Becoming part of a company that was awarded for its commitment to social good: We are one of 17 Ventures That Embody the U.N.’s 17 Sustainable Development Goals Inc. Magazine’s “Best in Business” Awardee in the software category for Companies That Put Purpose Before Profit Competitive compensation including equity A spacious office near Chancery Lane, where you can enjoy weekly team lunches Comprehensive health scheme offered through AXA Partnership with YellowNest, a salary exchange benefit that helps reduce childcare fees for working parents Cycle to Work Scheme - multiple options via Green Commute Initiative (GCI) Ready to join the ride? Via is an equal opportunity employer.
